candidates.text: While the Constitution diffuses power the better to secure liberty, it also contemplates that practice will integrate the dispersed powers into a workable government.
candidates.speaker: Jackson, concurring
phrases: diffuses power the better to secure liberty

candidates.text: The President's power, if any, to issue the order must stem either from an act of Congress or from the Constitution itself.
candidates.speaker: Black, for the Court

candidates.text: In the framework of our Constitution, the President's power to see that the laws are faithfully executed refutes the idea that he is to be a lawmaker.
candidates.speaker: Black, for the Court

candidates.text: In short, a systematic, unbroken, executive practice, long pursued to the knowledge of the Congress and never before questioned
candidates.speaker: Frankfurter, concurring

candidates.text: Under this messenger-boy concept of the Office, the President cannot even act to preserve legislative programs from destruction
